mainTopic: Using a כהן's share of קרבנות, or מעשר שני, for קידושין, and the פסוקים that show why these cannot be used.
overview: רבי יוחנן reports that the Sages voted and ruled that a כהן cannot make קידושין with his share of any קרבן. רב says the matter is still in dispute. אביי supports רבי יוחנן with a long ברייתא from the ספרא. Step by step, it teaches that כהנים may never trade their shares: not between different kinds of קרבנות, not between מנחות of the same kind, and not even in קדשים קלים. Since an unnamed ספרא follows רבי יהודה, even he agrees, which shows the dispute was settled. רבא tries to support רב from a ברייתא about greedy כהנים who 'take shares'. The גמרא answers that this means snatching, and explains the nickname 'בן חמצן' from two פסוקים. The גמרא then turns to the משנה about מעשר שני. It finds a source in the words 'קודש לה׳' and defends it against challenges from תרומת מעשר, חלה, שביעית and תרומה.

steps.title: The Sages voted: a כהן's portion cannot be used for קידושין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that the Sages counted votes and ruled that קידושין made with a כהן's share of קדשים does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: They counted votes and decided: one who betroths a woman with his portion, whether from the most holy offerings or from the lesser holy offerings, has not betrothed her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's report of a final vote of the Sages. They ruled that a כהן cannot make קידושין with his share of any קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier there was a dispute about this case. This vote settles it fully: no distinction between קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים. In both cases the קידושין does not take effect, like the view of רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: They counted votes and concluded, meaning a final group decision of the Sages
One who betroths with his share of the קרבנות
The most holy offerings
Offerings of lesser holiness

phrases.english: They counted and concluded:
phrases.notes: These are רבי יוחנן's words, reporting a vote the Sages took.

phrases.english: One who betroths a woman with his portion,
phrases.notes: His portion means the share a כהן gets from the קרבנות.

phrases.english: whether from the most holy offerings
or from the offerings of lesser holiness –
he has not betrothed her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from earlier in the daf about using a כהן's portion for קידושין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין with a כהן's portion of any type of קדשים is not valid.

steps.title: רב says the question was never settled
steps.stepSummary: רב disagrees with רבי יוחנן's report and says the matter is still a dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב says: It is still a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a different report: according to him, no final ruling was reached and the argument still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב does not argue about the logic. He argues about what actually happened: was there a vote or not? This leaves the question open, so the next step will try to decide which report is more likely.

keyTerms.meaning: Still, even now
A dispute between opinions

phrases.english: And רב says:
It is still a dispute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing report against רבי יוחנן's report of a final vote.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No final ruling was made; the dispute about קידושין with a כהן's portion remains open.

steps.title: אביי sides with רבי יוחנן and starts quoting a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רבי יוחנן's report makes more sense and brings a ברייתא: כהנים may not trade shares of מנחות for shares of animal זבחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It makes sense to follow רבי יוחנן. As it is taught in a ברייתא: From where do we know that כהנים do not trade shares of meal-offerings for animal offerings? The פסוק says: "And every meal-offering that is baked in the oven... shall be for all the sons of Aaron."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי decides between the two reports and supports רבי יוחנן. He begins a proof from a ברייתא about how כהנים divide their portions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the words "for all the sons of Aaron" that a מנחה must be divided among all the כהנים, and cannot be swapped for a share of an animal קרבן. This shows a כהן cannot do whatever he wants with his portion. The ברייתא continues for several more steps before the proof is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: Like him, following his view
It makes sense, it is reasonable
As it is taught in a ברייתא
Take shares, divide portions
Meal-offerings in exchange for animal offerings

steps.whyThisMatters: If כהנים may not trade their portions, it suggests they do not own them like regular property, which fits the ruling that a portion cannot be used for קידושין.

phrases.english: אביי said:
It is reasonable to follow רבי יוחנן,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
From where do we know that they do not take shares
of meal-offerings in exchange for animal offerings –
The פסוק says:
"And every meal-offering that is baked in the oven...
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:9

phrases.english: shall be for all the sons of Aaron."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:10

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the reports of steps 1 and 2 in favor of רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's report that the Sages ruled a כהן's portion cannot be used for קידושין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא learning from ויקרא 7:9-10 that כהנים may not trade shares of different קרבנות.

steps.title: Maybe מנחות can be traded for birds
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that even if מנחות can't be traded for animals, maybe they can be traded for birds, since a מנחה can replace a bird for a very poor person.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think they may not trade meal-offerings for animal offerings, since meal-offerings never replace them for a poor person. But they may trade meal-offerings for bird offerings, since meal-offerings do replace them for a poor person?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible exception to the rule it just taught. It is setting up the next פסוק to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals and מנחות have no link, since a מנחה never takes an animal's place. But birds and מנחות are linked: a very poor person who can't afford birds brings a מנחה instead. So maybe that link allows trading between them.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (a possible mistaken idea)
Bird offerings
Stood in their place, replaced them
Poverty

phrases.english: One might think they may not take shares
of meal-offerings in exchange for animal offerings,
since they do not replace them in a case of poverty,
phrases.notes: A poor person never brings a מנחה in place of an animal.

phrases.english: but they may take shares
of meal-offerings in exchange for bird offerings,
since they do replace them in a case of poverty?
phrases.notes: Someone too poor even for birds brings a מנחה instead.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יַחְלְקוּ מְנָחוֹת כְּנֶגֶד זְבָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how far the rule of step 3 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of the rule that מנחות may not be traded.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since מנחות replace birds for the poor, they are connected, so perhaps trading between them is allowed.

steps.title: A פסוק forbids trading מנחות for birds too
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings another phrase from the פסוק to show that מנחות may not be traded for birds either.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "And all that is made in the deep pan... shall be for all the sons of Aaron."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the suggestion from step 4 with a second phrase of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק repeats that this מנחה belongs to "all the sons of Aaron." That extra stress teaches that even the bird-and-מנחה link does not allow trading. Each מנחה is shared among all the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: A deep pan used for some מנחות
The פסוק teaches, introducing a source

phrases.english: The פסוק says:
"And all that is made in the deep pan...
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:9

phrases.english: shall be for all the sons of Aaron."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Derivation from an extra phrase in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מנחות could be traded for birds because they replace birds for the poor.
steps.terutzMaskana: מנחות may not be traded for birds either.

steps.title: Maybe birds can be traded for animals
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that birds and animal זבחים might be tradable, since both are blood offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think they may not trade meal-offerings for birds, since these are blood offerings and those are flour offerings. But they may trade birds for animal offerings, since both are blood offerings?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises another possible exception. It sets up the next phrase of the פסוק to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the reason מנחות can't be traded for birds is that they are a different kind: flour versus blood. Birds and animals are the same kind, since the blood of both goes on the מזבח. So maybe trading between them is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Types of offerings with blood put on the מזבח
Types of offerings made of flour
These

phrases.english: One might think they may not take shares
of meal-offerings in exchange for bird offerings,
since these are types of blood offerings
and those are types of flour offerings,
but they may take shares
of bird offerings in exchange for animal offerings,
since both these and those are types of blood offerings?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יַחְלְקוּ מְנָחוֹת כְּנֶגֶד עוֹפוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new reason for step 5's rule, which would allow a different trade.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether the no-trading rule covers birds and animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the problem is only mixing blood and flour, then birds and animals, both blood offerings, could be traded.

steps.title: "And on a griddle" forbids trading birds for animals
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא uses the words "and on a griddle" to teach that birds may not be traded for animal זבחים either.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "And on a griddle."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the last suggestion with one more phrase from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "and on a griddle" add another item to the list, and the ברייתא uses them to stretch the rule further. So far three trades are ruled out: מנחות for animals, מנחות for birds, and birds for animals. The ברייתא continues in the next steps with even closer pairings.

keyTerms.meaning: A flat griddle used for some מנחות

steps.whatToRemember: So far the ברייתא has ruled out three trades: מנחות for animals, מנחות for birds, and birds for animals. It keeps narrowing the case in the next steps, and אביי uses the whole ברייתא to support רבי יוחנן's report.

phrases.english: The פסוק says:
"And on a griddle."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:9. These extra words are what teach that birds can't be traded for animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Derivation from an extra phrase in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Birds and animals, both blood offerings, could be traded for each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bird offerings may not be traded for animal offerings either.

steps.title: Maybe meal-offerings can be traded for other meal-offerings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that even if birds can't be traded for animals, maybe one מנחה can be traded for another מנחה, since both are handled by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think: birds can't be traded for animal offerings, because birds are killed by hand and animals with a knife. But maybe meal-offerings can be traded for meal-offerings, since both are handled by hand?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא accepts that birds and animals can't be swapped. It then suggests a closer match: one מנחה for another מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Birds and animals were kept apart because they are handled differently: a bird's neck is pinched by hand, and an animal is slaughtered with a knife. Two מנחות are both handled by hand, so the ברייתא wonders if that closeness lets them be traded.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought (opens a suggestion that will be rejected)
They may take a share / trade shares
In exchange for
Their service is done by hand
With a utensil (here, a slaughtering knife)

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יַחְלְקוּ עוֹפוֹת כְּנֶגֶד זְבָחִים,
phrases.english: One might think they may not trade shares of birds for animal offerings,
since these are done by hand
phrases.notes: A bird offering is killed by pinching its neck by hand, with no knife.

phrases.english: and those are done with a utensil,
but maybe they may trade meal-offerings for meal-offerings,
since both these and those are done by hand?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יַחְלְקוּ עוֹפוֹת כְּנֶגֶד זְבָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 7's result (birds not for animals) and suggests a closer pairing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that no shares may ever be traded
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason against trading is a difference in how offerings are handled, then two offerings handled the same way should be tradable.

steps.title: The פסוק says every meal-offering belongs to all the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The words "every meal-offering mixed with oil, to all the sons of Aaron" show that one מנחה may not be traded for another.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: "And every meal-offering mixed with oil shall belong to all the sons of Aaron."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with the next phrase of the פסוק: even מנחה for מנחה may not be traded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "To all the sons of Aaron" means each מנחה is divided among all the כהנים of the shift. Since every כהן has a part in every מנחה, no כהן can trade away his share of one מנחה for a share of another.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces a פסוק that settles the question)
Mixed with oil
The sons of Aaron, meaning the כהנים

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And every meal-offering mixed with oil
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:10

phrases.english: shall belong to all the sons of Aaron."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וְכׇל מִנְחָה בְלוּלָה בַשֶּׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8's suggestion with a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Meal-offerings, all handled by hand, might be tradable for each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Every מנחה belongs to all the כהנים, so מנחה may not be traded for מנחה.

steps.title: Maybe griddle can be traded for griddle, and pan for pan
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that even if a griddle מנחה can't be traded for a deep-pan מנחה, maybe identical types can be traded.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think: a griddle offering can't be traded for a deep-pan offering, or the other way around, because one comes out soft and the other hard. But maybe griddle can be traded for griddle, and deep-pan for deep-pan, since both are hard, or both are soft?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא narrows the case even more: two מנחות of the exact same kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחבת (flat griddle) makes a hard product, and a מרחשת (deep pan) makes a soft one, so mixing those two seems clearly not allowed. But when both are the very same type, they are identical, so maybe trading is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: A flat griddle; a מנחה made on it comes out hard
A deep pan; a מנחה made in it comes out soft
Soft
Hard
Or else / alternatively

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יַחְלְקוּ מַחֲבַת כְּנֶגֶד מַרְחֶשֶׁת
phrases.english: One might think they may not trade a griddle offering for a deep-pan offering
or a deep-pan offering for a griddle offering,
since this one comes out soft
phrases.notes: "This one" is the deep pan, and "that one" in the next line is the griddle.

phrases.english: and that one comes out hard,
but maybe they may trade griddle for griddle
and deep-pan for deep-pan,
since both of these come out hard,
or else both come out soft?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יַחְלְקוּ מַחֲבַת כְּנֶגֶד מַרְחֶשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 9 for different kinds of מנחות and suggests identical kinds.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that no מנחה may be traded for another
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two מנחות of exactly the same kind are identical, so trading them should change nothing.

steps.title: The word "dry" shows that even identical types can't be traded
steps.stepSummary: The words "or dry, shall belong to all the sons of Aaron" teach that even griddle for griddle or pan for pan may not be traded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: "Or dry, it shall belong to all the sons of Aaron."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with another phrase of the same פסוק: even two מנחות of the very same kind may not be traded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק repeats "to all the sons of Aaron" for this kind of מנחה too. That repetition shows that even when two offerings are exactly alike, each one still belongs to all the כהנים, so there is nothing private to trade.

keyTerms.meaning: Dry, meaning a מנחה without oil mixed in

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"Or dry, it shall belong to all the sons of Aaron."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:10

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וַחֲרֵבָה לְכׇל בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן תִּהְיֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10's suggestion with a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Identical types of מנחה might be tradable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even identical types may not be traded.

steps.title: Maybe offerings of lesser holiness can be traded
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that the ban on trading may apply only to קדשי קדשים, and not to קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think: they may not trade shares of the most holy offerings, but they may trade shares of offerings of lesser holiness?
steps.whatsHappening: Everything so far was about the most holy offerings. Now the ברייתא asks if the less holy offerings might be different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחות discussed so far are קדשי קדשים, which have stricter rules. קדשים קלים are less strict, so maybe trading shares of them is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the highest holiness (like מנחות and חטאות)
Offerings of lesser holiness (like a תודה or שלמים)

phrases.english: One might think they may not trade shares of the most holy offerings
but they may trade shares of offerings of lesser holiness?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the details of מנחות to a different level of holiness.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying the no-trading rule to all offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The strict rule might come from the high holiness of קדשי קדשים, so less holy offerings might be more flexible.

steps.title: The נסמך פסוק of תודה shows lesser offerings are the same
steps.stepSummary: From "one like his brother" and the next פסוק about a תודה, the ברייתא learns that קדשים קלים also can't be traded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: "One like his brother," and right next to it: "If for a thanks-offering." Just as shares of the most holy offerings may not be traded, so shares of offerings of lesser holiness may not be traded.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers by linking two פסוקים that sit side by side, so the rule of the most holy offerings carries over to the less holy ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "One like his brother" closes the פסוק about מנחות, and right after it the תורה starts talking about a תודה, which is a קדשים קלים. Because they are placed next to each other, the no-trading rule moves from the first to the second.

keyTerms.meaning: One like his brother; each כהן gets an equal share
Right next to it (a פסוק placed nearby)
A thanks-offering, one of the קדשים קלים
Just as... so too

steps.whatToRemember: Step by step, the ברייתא closes every opening: no trading of shares, whether between types, within the same type, or even in קדשים קלים.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "One like his brother,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:10

phrases.english: and right next to it: "If for a thanks-offering" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:12. A תודה is a less holy offering, which is why this link matters.

phrases.english: just as they may not trade shares of the most holy offerings,
so they may not trade shares of offerings of lesser holiness.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: אִישׁ כְּאָחִיו וּסְמִיךְ לֵיהּ: אִם עַל תּוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by linking nearby פסוקים.
steps.terutzMaskana: קדשים קלים follow the same rule: no trading of shares.

steps.title: An adult כהן gets a share even with a blemish, a minor does not
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the word "אִישׁ" that an adult כהן receives a share even if blemished, but a minor does not, even if unblemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: "A man": a man receives a share, even if he has a blemish. But a minor does not receive a share, even if he has no blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more teaching from the same words: who gets a portion at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "אִישׁ" means an adult. So the key is age, not physical fitness: a בעל מום, who can't serve, still eats, while a קטן does not get a share.

keyTerms.meaning: Receives a share (here: gets a portion in the division)
A כהן with a physical blemish who may not serve
A minor
Unblemished, physically whole

steps.confusionAlert: Here "חוֹלֵק" means getting a portion in the division, not trading one share for another as in the earlier steps.

phrases.english: "A man": a man receives a share,
even one with a blemish,
but a minor does not receive a share
even if he is unblemished.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישׁ אִישׁ חוֹלֵק אֲפִילּוּ בַּעַל מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a further teaching from the word "אִישׁ" quoted in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An adult כהן receives a share even with a blemish; a minor does not, even if unblemished.

steps.title: Whose view is an unnamed ספרא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the author is behind an unattributed teaching in the ספרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is an unattributed ספרא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its point: it asks whose opinion this ברייתא from the ספרא follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא quoted is from the ספרא and gives no name. Finding its author will let the גמרא link this ruling to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: An unattributed teaching in the ספרא, the מדרש on ויקרא
Whose is it? / Who is the author?

phrases.english: Whose view is an unattributed ספרא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the content of the ברייתא back to אביי's proof from step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The author of the unnamed ספרא.

steps.title: It is רבי יהודה, so רבי יוחנן's report is proven
steps.stepSummary: The unnamed ספרא is רבי יהודה, who rules that there is no trading of shares at all. This supports רבי יוחנן's report that the Sages settled the matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה, and he says that there is no law of trading shares at all. Conclude from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ספרא follows רבי יהודה, and that settles אביי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If כהנים can never trade their shares, then the share isn't treated as the כהן's own property, so it can't be used for קידושין. Since this unnamed ספרא is רבי יהודה, who had disagreed earlier, it shows he too came to accept רבי יוסי's view. That supports רבי יוחנן's report that the Sages voted and settled the matter.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of trading shares
At all
Conclude from it; the proof stands

steps.whatToRemember: Since the unnamed ספרא is רבי יהודה and he allows no trading at all, even רבי יהודה agrees that a כהן does not own his share in a way that can be used for קידושין. This supports רבי יוחנן's report that the Sages voted and settled the question.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes אביי's proof from step 3 and shows that רבי יוחנן's report of a final vote is more likely than רב's claim that the dispute continues.

phrases.english: It is רבי יהודה,
and he says
that there is no law of trading shares at all.
Conclude from it.
phrases.notes: Conclude that even רבי יהודה agrees, so רבי יוחנן's report that the Sages settled it is right.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְהוּא קָאָמַר דְּלֵית בַּהּ דִּין חֲלוּקָהּ כְּלָל שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 and completes אביי's proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The unnamed ספרא is רבי יהודה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה holds there is no trading of shares at all, so even he agrees a כהן cannot use his share for קידושין. This supports רבי יוחנן's report that the Sages voted and settled the matter.

steps.title: רבא brings a ברייתא that seems to support רב
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא: modest כהנים hold back, while greedy כהנים 'take shares'. This seems to show that portions can be divided by the כהנים' own choice, which would support רב's claim that the matter is still in dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Isn't there a ברייתא that matches רב? It teaches: the modest כהנים pull back their hands, and the greedy ones take the shares.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a proof for רב's opinion from a ברייתא about how כהנים behaved when portions were handed out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the greedy ones 'חולקים', which sounds like they take shares with permission. If so, the shares can be handed around by the כהנים' own choice, as if they own them. That would mean the strict view never won out, which supports רב's claim that the dispute is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: Modest, refined people
Gluttons, greedy eaters
Take shares, divide
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: Rava said:
But isn't it taught in line with Rav?
phrases.notes: רב said the question was still in dispute, so a source that treats the shares as the כהנים' own would back him.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
the modest ones withdraw their hands,
and the gluttons take shares.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ספרא was shown to follow רבי יהודה, רבא brings a ברייתא that seems to back רב's opposing view.
steps.raayaObject: רב's report that the question is still in dispute and was not settled against ownership of the shares
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'the modest withdraw their hands and the gluttons take shares'

steps.title: 'Taking shares' really means snatching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'חולקים' means the greedy ones grabbed. The end of the same ברייתא proves it: one man grabbed his friend's share and was nicknamed 'בן חמצן' for life.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'take shares' mean? They snatched. We see this from the end of that ברייתא: a man once grabbed his own share and his friend's share, and people called him 'son of the snatcher' until the day he died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof. The ברייתא describes wrongful grabbing, not permitted dividing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'חולקים' meant a permitted division, the ברייתא would not call the greedy ones by an insulting nickname. The ending shows the act was considered shameful snatching, so it is no proof for רב.

keyTerms.meaning: They snatch, grab
The latter part of a teaching
'Son of the snatcher', an insulting nickname

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not describing an allowed custom. Its own ending shows that the greedy כהנים were being criticized.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about the greedy כהנים is not a proof for רב, because 'חולקים' means snatching.

phrases.english: What is "take shares"? They snatch,
as it teaches in the latter clause:
An incident with one who snatched
his share and his colleague's share,
and they would call him:
"Ben Chamtzan" until the day he died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof by reading 'חולקים' as snatching.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof for רב from the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'חולקים' means grabbing, as the end of the ברייתא shows, not permitted division.

steps.title: A פסוק showing that 'חומץ' means a grabber
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא brings a פסוק from תהלים where 'חומץ' is listed with the wicked and the unjust, showing the word means one who grabs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב שילא said: Which פסוק shows this meaning? 'My God, save me from the hand of the wicked, from the grip of the unjust and the grabber (חומץ).'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב שילא asks and answers his own question: where do we see that 'חמצן' means a snatcher?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, 'חומץ' appears next to 'רשע' and 'מעוול', words for people who do wrong. So 'חומץ', and the nickname 'חמצן', describe someone who takes what is not his.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק (source)?
An unjust person
A grabber, a robber

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא: מַאי קְרָאָה?

steps.title: A second פסוק for the meaning of 'חמוץ'
steps.stepSummary: רבה brings a different פסוק, from ישעיהו: 'אשרו חמוץ', meaning help the one who was robbed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: We learn it from here: 'Learn to do good, seek justice, help the one who was robbed (חמוץ).'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה offers another פסוק that shows the same meaning of the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'חמוץ' is the victim whose things were grabbed. So the root חמץ is about grabbing or robbing, which again explains the nickname 'בן חמצן'.

keyTerms.meaning: From here
Help the one who was robbed

"Learn to do well, seek justice,

phrases.notes: 'חמוץ' here is the person who was robbed, so the word is about grabbing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק for the same meaning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'חמוץ' in ישעיהו refers to a robbery victim, so the root means grabbing.
steps.whatToRemember: 'בן חמצן' means 'son of the snatcher'. Two different פסוקים show that the root חמץ is about grabbing.

steps.title: The משנה about betrothing with מעשר שני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. רבי מאיר says betrothal with מעשר שני never works. רבי יהודה says it fails if done by mistake but works if done on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone betroths with מעשר שני, whether by mistake or on purpose, it is not a betrothal; these are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: by mistake, no betrothal; on purpose, it is a betrothal, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, about מעשר שני. This quote sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two תנאים argue over whether מעשר שני can be used for קידושין. רבי מאיר's view, that it never works, will need a source.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, produce that must be eaten in ירושלים
Unintentionally, by mistake
Intentionally, on purpose
He betrothed (the קידושין works)

phrases.english: Second tithe, whether unwittingly or intentionally —

steps.title: What is the source for רבי מאיר's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that מעשר שני cannot be used for קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי מאיר's rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says betrothal with מעשר שני fails even when done on purpose. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that מעשר שני cannot be used for קידושין.

steps.title: 'It is the Lord's' and not for betrothing a woman
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא, quoting a received tradition, learns from 'לַה׳ הוּא' in the פסוק about מעשר that it belongs to ה׳ and cannot be used to betroth a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said in the name of tradition: The פסוק says, 'All the tithe of the land, from the seed of the land and the fruit of the tree, is the Lord's; it is holy to the Lord.' It is the Lord's, and not for betrothing a woman with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא answers the question with a פסוק about מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לַה׳ הוּא' show that the produce belongs to ה׳ in a special way. So a man cannot give it as his own to make a betrothal.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of the received tradition
It is the Lord's
To betroth a woman with it

steps.whyThisMatters: This source becomes the test case for the next challenges, which ask why other holy items with similar wording can be used for קידושין.

phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said
in the name of tradition:
"And all the tithe of the land, of the seed of the land,

phrases.english: It is for the Lord, and not for betrothing a woman with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּגְמָרָא

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'לַה׳ הוּא' in ויקרא 27:30: מעשר is ה׳'s and not for betrothing a woman.

steps.title: Challenge from תרומת מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about תרומת מעשר also calls it 'תרומת ה׳', yet a משנה rules that betrothal with תרומה works. So why should 'לה׳' rule out betrothal with מעשר שני?
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at תרומת מעשר, where it is written: 'So you too shall set apart the gift of the Lord.' And we learned in a משנה: one who betroths with תרומה, the woman is betrothed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source just given, using another holy gift that is also linked to ה׳'s name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If belonging to ה׳ blocks קידושין, then תרומת מעשר, called 'תרומת ה׳', should not work either. Yet the משנה says betrothal with תרומה does work. So mentioning ה׳ cannot be enough to block it.

The gift of produce given to a כהן

steps.title: תרומת מעשר does not say 'לַה׳'
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the פסוק about תרומת מעשר does not use the exact word 'לַה׳', so the source's reasoning does not apply to it.

steps.deeperAnalysis: The source rests on the specific word 'לַה׳', 'belonging to ה׳'. The פסוק about תרומת מעשר says 'תרומת ה׳', 'the gift of ה׳', and not 'לַה׳'. So the rule against betrothal does not cover it.

keyTerms.meaning: Because it is not written about it

steps.title: Challenge from חלה, which is also 'given to ה׳'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that חלה is described in the תורה as given 'לה׳', yet a משנה rules that betrothing with תרומות (which include חלה) works.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about חלה? The פסוק says 'you shall give it to ה׳'. And yet we learned in the משנה that a man who betroths a woman with תרומות makes a valid betrothal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source for why מעשר שני can't be used for קידושין. It brings חלה, which is also called 'לה׳' but still works for betrothal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the word 'לה׳' alone were enough to stop קידושין, then חלה should not work either. But the משנה says betrothing with תרומות works, and that includes חלה. So the reasoning from 'לה׳' seems too broad.

steps.title: That פסוק is about the Jewish people, not תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק in ירמיהו describes the Jewish people as holy to ה׳. It is not describing תרומה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: That one (that פסוק)
Israel is holy, describing the Jewish people

steps.whatToRemember: מעשר שני cannot be used for קידושין because its פסוק calls it both 'קודש' and 'לה׳'. תרומת מעשר lacks 'לה׳', חלה has only 'לה׳', שביעית has only 'קודש', and the פסוק in ירמיהו is about the Jewish people, not תרומה. So all of these still work for קידושין.

phrases.english: That verse is written about the Jewish people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from תרומה and closes this round of challenges.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the subject of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק in ירמיהו calls תרומה 'holy to ה׳'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק describes the Jewish people, so תרומה is not called 'קודש לה׳' and works for קידושין.
